questions.prompt_text: Consider the following 3×3 matrix, which represents the RGB values corresponding to Figure 1. questions.prompt_text: A university office is preparing to scan and store three documents: a black-and-white attendance sheet, a colored event photo, and a student's ID card scan. The university authority has decided to prepare a report for technical specifications and future reusability, the report should i) explain the different types of digital images that may correspond to the files described above, ii) explain the technique used for representing digital images in computers, and iii) state the commonly used digital image formats suitable for storing and processing each of the above files.
questions.criteria: Clear explanation of different types of digital images, technique for representing digital images, and suitable digital image formats
questions.ideal_answer: The report should clearly explain the different types of digital images, technique for representing digital images, and suitable digital image formats for each document

questions.prompt_text: Digital Image Processing consists of five fundamental steps: Image Formation, Image Acquisition, Image Transformation, Feature Selection, and Classification. questions.criteria: Clear explanation of core principles of Image Transformation and Feature Selection, and analysis of commonly used techniques and their applications
questions.ideal_answer: The core principles of Image Transformation and Feature Selection should be explained, and the commonly used techniques and their applications should be analyzed

reading_order.text: IUBAT School of Computer Science and Engineering
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Mid Term Examination of Summer Semester 2026
Program: Bachelor of Computer Science and Engineering (BCSE)

Course Code: CSE 4385
Time: 01 Hour 30 Minutes

Course Title: Computer Vision and Image Processing
Full Marks: 100

Instructions:
1. Answer all the questions.  2. Marks allocated are indicated in the right margin.

1. Consider the 8-bit grayscale image shown in Figure 1, represented by the matrix given beside. Apply the
histogram equalization shifting technique to this image and determine the resulting pixel value of the 3rd row
after the transformation. [CO2, C3, PO1 — 25 marks]
Figure 1: Football Ground and Corresponding Image Matrix

2. Consider the following 3×3 matrix, which represents the RGB values corresponding to Figure 1. Convert
the RGB value of the first pixel of the matrix into its equivalent HSI (Hue, Saturation, Intensity) and CMY
(Cyan, Magenta, Yellow) representations. Justify your answer with an appropriate mathematical derivation.
[CO2, C3, PO1 — 15 + 10 = 25 marks]

3. A university office is preparing to scan and store three documents: a black-and-white attendance sheet, a
colored event photo, and a student's ID card scan. The university authority has decided to prepare a report
for technical specifications and future reusability, the report should i) explain the different types of digital
images that may correspond to the files described above, ii) explain the technique used for representing
digital images in computers, and iii) state the commonly used digital image formats suitable for storing and
processing each of the above files. Write and prepare the report for the university. [CO1, C2, PO1 — 8 + 10
+ 7 = 25 marks]

4. Digital Image Processing consists of five fundamental steps: Image Formation, Image Acquisition, Image
Transformation, Feature Selection, and Classification. Briefly explain the core principles of Image
Transformation and Feature Selection, and analyze the commonly used techniques and their applications in
enhancing image analysis, pattern recognition, and classification tasks associated with these two steps.
[CO1, C2, PO1 — 10 + 15 = 25 marks]
Bloom's Taxonomy Levels in Cognitive Domain:
C1: Remember; C2: Understand; C3: Apply; C4: Analyze; C5: Evaluate; C6: Create

CO1: Apply digital image processing techniques and computer vision algorithms to solve image analysis,
identification, recognition, segmentation, detection, and classification operations.

CO2: Explain the fundamental concepts of computer vision and digital image processing for optimized
solution, interpretation, and decision making.

PO1: Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering
specialization as specified in K1 to K4 respectively to the solution of complex engineering problems.
